question: The system prompt of your customer support agent holds several rules. Your team wants to move one of these rules out of the prompt and into a programmatic check in code. In testing, the agent follows each prompt rule in most conversations, but in a small share of conversations it skips a rule. Which rule most needs a programmatic check?

options.text: Keep each reply to the customer under 150 words unless the customer asks for more detail.
options.reason: An occasional long reply is harmless, so this rule does not need deterministic compliance and prompt guidance is enough.

options.text: Send each refund only to the payment method of the original order, as legal policy requires.
options.reason: This financial rule requires deterministic compliance, and prompt instructions alone have a non-zero failure rate, so only a programmatic check in code can guarantee it every time.

options.text: Offer a short apology when lookup_order shows that a delivery arrived late.
options.reason: A rare missed apology does not break a policy that must hold every time, so a prompt instruction with a small failure rate is acceptable here.

options.text: Greet each customer by first name, using the name that get_customer returns.
options.reason: A rare missed greeting causes no compliance or financial harm, so this style rule does not need deterministic compliance and can stay as prompt guidance.
